Title: AG-C: Nicky Liow paid RM10m compound before money laundering charges withdrawn
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Nicky Liow Soon Hee paid a RM10 million compound in 2023 before the Attorney General's Chambers (A-GC) withdrew 26 money laundering charges against him.
In a statement today, the A-GC said the decision was made after carefully considering representations submitted by Liow's lawyers, Messrs Rajpal, Firah & Vishnu.
The representations, dated Dec 15, 2022 and April 6, 2023, sought for the 26 charges under Section 4 of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 to be compounded under Section 92 of the same Act.
"After reviewing the representations and the available evidence, the A-GC agreed to offer a RM10 million compound, which Liow agreed and paid on May 29, 2023.
"Apart from the RM10 million compound, settlement also included the forfeiture of a RM647,366 bond as well as the forfeiture of assets that had been seized.
"Following payment of the compound, the prosecution withdrew all 26 charges against Liow in accordance with Section 92.
"On June 15, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court ordered Liow to be discharged and acquitted of all the charges," it said.

Title: Three held over syndicate creating fake passport movement records for RM700
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has crippled a "flying passport" syndicate that allegedly created fake movement records by processing foreign passports without their owners being present at entry points.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said three suspects, aged between 33 and 41, were arrested yesterday in a special operation at Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB), Gelang Patah, Johor.
He said the arrests were made following investigations under Op Crack, which was conducted in collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
"The syndicate's modus operandi involved collecting passports belonging to foreigners without requiring the physical presence of the document owners at the country's entry points.
"Copies of the front pages of the passports were then sent by the syndicate's agents through WhatsApp to individuals working with the syndicate to be scanned, creating fake movement records in the Immigration Department's system," he said in a statement.
Zakaria said the syndicate charged RM700 for each foreign passport processed through the illegal service.
During the operation, enforcement personnel seized several items believed to be linked to the syndicate's activities, including mobile phones, premises keys, jewellery, immigration security stamps and RM20,000 in cash.
He said all three suspects were detained for alleged offences under Section 12(1)(h) of the Passport Act for unlawful possession, control or retention of travel documents and were taken to the Immigration Office for further action.
The operation involved officers from the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division at its headquarters in Putrajaya, together with Johor Immigration Department personnel.
Zakaria said the department would continue comprehensive investigations to identify the syndicate's network and take action against any activities that violate the country's laws.

Title: Tropicana builds Langkawi portfolio with six projects, taps foreign demand
Article:
LANGKAWI: Tropicana Corp Bhd is building up in Langkawi, Kedah, with six development projects backed by a land bank spanning about 730 hectares, positioning the property developer to tap into growing demand for resort-style living, hospitality and tourism-led real estate on the island.
The company, currently the largest developer in Langkawi, is developing an integrated lifestyle ecosystem across key tourism locations, including Pantai Cenang, Tanjung Rhu and Pantai Kok, combining residential, hospitality and commercial offerings to attract both lifestyle buyers and investors.
Tropicana is also exploring future developments near Bandar Padang Lalang, Padang Matsirat and Pulau Rebak Kecil, as it strengthens its long-term commitment to Langkawi's tourism potential and supports Langkawi's evolution as a premium lifestyle destination.
"For more than four decades, Tropicana has been creating vibrant communities where people aspire to live. Today, we are taking the next step by creating destinations where people aspire to stay, explore and return to," Tropicana managing director of marketing, sales and business development, Ixora Ang.
At the centre of its Langkawi expansion is Tropicana Cenang, a 2.14ha freehold beachfront integrated development in Pantai Cenang comprising serviced residences, retail outlets and hospitality components.
The development has gained strong market traction, with its first two phases, Assana Serviced Suites and Merissa Serviced Suites, fully sold.
Launched in September 2021, the first phase, Assana, comprises a 39-storey tower with 831 serviced suites and recorded strong demand, with Malaysians accounting for about 85 per cent of buyers. Units were launched from RM500,000.
The second phase, Merissa Serviced Suites, was launched in June 2023 with a gross development value (GDV) of RM115 million. The beachfront project comprises 60 units with built-up sizes ranging from 1,066 sq ft to 1,303 sq ft, with launch prices starting from RM1.71 million.
Both Assana and Merissa were completed in April this year, marking the first completed residential components under the broader Tropicana Cenang master plan.
The final phase, Clarissa Serviced Suites, has achieved about 20 per cent take-up since its launch in April last year, Ang said.
Ang said the company plans to further expand its Langkawi portfolio through future projects, including Tropicana Lagoon (Tanjung Rhu) and Tropicana Shores (Pantai Kok).
[[nid:1506101]]
Speaking on the sidelines of the launch of the T Journey Hospitality app at Assana, she said buyer profiles have shifted across the development phases, with Clarissa attracting stronger interest from foreign purchasers compared with the earlier phases.
She said the growing international participation reflects rising interest in Langkawi's premium beachfront property market.
With a GDV of RM922.6 million, the freehold 40-storey Clarissa will comprise 806 fully furnished serviced suites with built-up areas ranging from 536 sq ft to 1,356 sq ft. Prices start from RM668,800 and exceed RM1 million for selected units.
The launch of T Journey Hospitality also marks Tropicana's entry into hospitality operations at Tropicana Cenang.
The digital platform will serve as an integrated hospitality management and guest services ecosystem, supporting property owners while enhancing visitor experiences across Tropicana's developments. The group plans to expand the platform to future projects in Langkawi, Genting Highlands and Johor.
The launch also marked a strategic collaboration with AirAsia Rewards as T Journey's inaugural launch partner, alongside 10 other partners, including the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, the Langkawi Development Authority, Dream Forest Langkawi, Underwater World Langkawi, Langkawi Wildlife Park, Crocodile Adventureland Langkawi, Sedunia Travel Services, Mitra Malaysia and HostPlatform.

Title: Rising costs top Singapore businesses' concerns, survey finds
Article:
SINGAPORE: Rising business costs have become the biggest concern for Singapore companies as geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty weigh on sentiment, a survey by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry has shown, reported Xinhua.
According to the survey released on Wednesday, the most commonly cited concern was rising business costs, selected by 71.8 per cent of respondents. The other top concerns were the availability of suitable manpower and business transformation to capture new growth opportunities.
The ongoing conflict in West Asia has added to business uncertainty, with respondents identifying higher operating costs, market uncertainty, weaker demand and supply chain disruptions as the main risks.
Businesses also turned more cautious about the outlook. Thirty-eight per cent of respondents were neutral on business prospects, while 34 per cent were pessimistic and only 20 per cent were optimistic.
Reflecting the subdued sentiment, only 34 per cent of businesses expect revenue to grow this year, down from 39 per cent in 2025. Although 78 per cent still expect to remain profitable, more than half of them anticipate lower profits than last year.
The survey also showed Malaysia, Indonesia, China, Vietnam and Thailand emerged as the top overseas markets for expansion.
Meanwhile, 45 per cent of respondents said they were experimenting with off-the-shelf artificial intelligence tools, although limited expertise and implementation costs remain key barriers to wider adoption.

Title: Gold heads for best week since January; US jobs data in focus
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold prices firmed on Friday and were on track for their biggest weekly gain since January, helped by weaker oil prices, while investors awaited key US nonfarm payrolls data for clues on the interest rate outlook.
Spot gold was up 0.6 per cent at US$4,262.39 per ounce, as of 0421 GMT after hitting a seven-week high on Thursday. Prices were up over 5 per cent for the week.
US gold futures gained 0.5 per cent to US$4,321.50.
Hopes of peace in the Middle East saw inflation expectations drop, allowing gold to surge higher from a multi-week consolidation above US$4,000, said Matt Simpson, a senior analyst at StoneX.
US President Donald Trump told reporters that he believed the war with Iran would be over soon and said the armed forces were experiencing issues with supplies of some weapons.
Crude oil prices were headed for a weekly loss. Lower energy prices help ease inflation concerns and reduce expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates. Gold is an inflation hedge, but elevated interest rates tend to weigh on its appeal as it offers no yield.
The US Labor Department's nonfarm payrolls report for July is due at 1230 GMT.
"Regardless of how NFP plays out, US$4,000 has proven to be a solid support level - and I suspect bulls are waiting for dips to take advantage of a much-needed correction higher towards US$4,600. NFP may provide some noise over the near term, but price action has spoken, and gold looks like it wants to rally," Simpson added.
Traders currently see a 55 per cent chance of a US rate hike in September, from 63 per cent a week ago, per the CME FedWatch Tool.
"Going into August, we are somewhat friendlier towards gold and expect a wider trading band to set in," Marex said in a monthly note.
Spot silver added 1.3 per cent to US$62.27, platinum rose 0.5 per cent to US$1,737.25, while palladium dropped 0.2 per cent to US$1,368.37. All three metals were headed for weekly gains.

Title: Nurul Izzah's resignation reflects PKR turmoil, says Pas
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas believes Nurul Izzah Anwar's resignation as PKR deputy president reflects serious internal problems within the ruling party.
Its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the deputy president's role was crucial, particularly when the party president was occupied with his duties as prime minister.
"When a deputy president resigns, it will certainly have an impact on the party.
"In a situation where the president is busy with his responsibilities as prime minister, it is the deputy president who is supposed to manage party affairs.
"Pas believes the resignation reflects internal divisions that have surfaced in recent months.
"We believe there is internal turmoil in PKR. What we are seeing began with protests from within the party itself," he told reporters at Medan Ilmu here today.
The Perikatan Nasional deputy chairman said reports involving several PKR members of parliament had further fuelled the unrest.
"More recently, reports emerged that MPs from Ampang, Subang and several other constituencies had their allocations withheld even though they are from the same party.
"If a party is withholding allocations from its own elected representatives, it suggests the internal conflict is very serious," he said.
The Kubang Kerian MP said the developments seen publicly could be only a reflection of deeper issues within the party.
"What we see from the outside may only be a reflection. Internally, we believe the problems could be much bigger.
"Why would members of the same party have their allocations withheld? It points to weaknesses in the party's leadership and organisation.
"It could also stem from internal clashes dating back to the period when Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli was still in the party leadership," he said.
However, Tuan Ibrahim stressed that PKR's internal affairs were ultimately for the party to resolve.
"That is their internal matter. However, from the people's perspective, PKR is the ruling party.
"Whatever decisions it makes within the party will have a direct impact on the people," he said.
Nurul Izzah
announced yesterday
that she was relinquishing the PKR deputy presidency after careful consideration to focus on her studies while continuing to serve society beyond the political sphere.
In a Facebook post, she said she would remain a PKR member and continue supporting the party's efforts to build a better Malaysia.

Title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday amid mixed regional markets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia remained lower at midday, tracking mixed performances across regional markets as investor sentiment remained cautious amid concerns over rising oil prices, driven by the ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
At 12.30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 1.17 points to 1,735.98 from Thursday's close of 1,737.15.
The benchmark index opened 1.93 points lower at 1,735.22, and fluctuated between 1,729.34 and 1,739.14 during the morning trading session.
On the broader market, losers outpaced gainers 558 to 379, while 560 counters were unchanged, 1,276 untraded and 21 suspended.
Turnover totalled 1.96 billion units, worth RM1.66 billion.
Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said the FBM KLCI is expected to trade on a mixed footing today.
"Spiking crude oil prices, driven by Middle East supply disruptions, will continue to provide immediate trading catalysts across energy counters.
"However, strong fundamental catalysts should continue to support resilience in technology counters," it said in a note today.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Public Bank dropped eight sen to RM10.72 and RM5.15, respectively, CIMB Group lost six sen to RM7.91, and IHH Healthcare eased two sen to RM8.31, while Public Bank added six sen to RM14.54.
Of the active stocks, Perak Transit gained four sen to 21.5 sen, YTL Corp climbed 16 sen to RM2.13, and YTL Power International was 29 sen stronger at RM4.66, while Malaysian Resources Corp and HHRG were flat at 34 sen and 10.5 sen, respectively.
Nestle led the gainers list, jumping 60 sen to RM101.90, while Tong Herr Resources strengthened 49 sen to RM2.39, Hong Leong Industries went up 24 sen to RM17.92, and Allianz Malaysia grew by 20 sen to RM21.28.
As for the top losers, Batu Kawan slumped 66 sen to RM20.74, Malaysian Pacific Industries shed 42 sen to RM47.24, United Plantations fell 32 sen to RM33.88, and UMS Integration slid 19 sen to RM7.56.
Among the broader indices, the FBM Emas Index shed 15.44 points to 12,840.57, the FBM Top 100 Index erased 16.25 points to 12,669.03, and the FBM Mid 70 Index contracted 56.31 points to 18,269.75.
The FBM ACE Index put on 23.15 points to 5,060.90, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index inched up 0.57 of a point to 12,692.11.
Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index dropped 144.19 points to 20,375.65, the Plantation Index shrank 25.06 points to 9,439.49, and the Energy Index retreated 3.34 points to 759.07, while the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.41 of a point to 188.19.

Title: Singapore banks ride Asia's wealth boom to weather rates headwind
Article:
SINGAPORE: A surge in income from wealth management and other fee revenue helped Singapore's top three banks to cushion the impact of low interest rates, as lenders bet the region's fast-growing affluent population will continue to underpin growth this year.
The results underscore the strength of Asia's wealth boom, which continues to drive regional lenders' earnings despite geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in global markets, as inflows into safe-haven financial hubs like Singapore and booming regional equity markets swell the ranks of Asia's rich.
OCBC, Singapore's second-largest bank, said on Friday its April-June net profit jumped 22 per cent to S$2.22 billion (US$1.73 billion), well above estimates, while UOB's net profit was up 10 per cent to S$1.5 billion, beating forecasts.
Shares of OCBC climbed three per cent to a record high of S$30.19, while UOB's fell more than two per cent at one point. The benchmark stock index rose 0.7 per cent.
Wealth management income for OCBC rose to a record high of S$3.29 billion in the first half, while UOB's hit an all-time peak of S$717 million, mirroring a trend seen across results from Singapore's biggest bank, DBS, and Asia-focused rivals HSBC and Standard Chartered earlier this week.
For the Singapore banks, that helped offset pressure from lower interest rates on their core lending operations.
All three banks reported lower second-quarter net interest margins, a key measure of lending profitability that reflects the difference between what banks earn on loans and pay for deposits and other funding.
In its annual report released last month, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said total assets under management in Singapore rose 10.1 per cent to S$6.7 trillion as at the end of 2025, helped in part by the country's status as a "trusted and attractive wealth management centre".
UOB UNDERPERFORMS PEERS
UOB cut its fee-income growth guidance for the year to the low single digits from high single digits the previous quarter, bucking the more upbeat momentum its peers DBS and OCBC expect for the rest of the year.
Chief Financial Officer Leong Yung Chee attributed the revision to the delay of some "sizeable deals" and lower-than-expected credit card fee income.
Trading and investment income for Singapore's third-largest bank also declined 8 per cent year-on-year to S$379 million, owing to lower trading and liquidity management activities.
UOB's growth in its key Southeast Asian markets of Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam cushioned its bottom line, as customer flows and intra-regional business activity continue to gather pace.
"We see healthy trade and investment flow, stronger connectivity with Greater China and ongoing supply chain shifts into the region, as businesses look to ASEAN for growth and diversification," said CEO Wee Ee Cheong at a media briefing.
"ASEAN is our home ground, our competitive advantage and our engine of growth."
UNCERTAIN MACRO BACKDROP
OCBC's non-interest income rose 51 per cent to S$1.91 billion in the second quarter, driven by a 28 per cent rise in fees, an 85 per cent jump in trading income and a 68 per cent increase in insurance income.
However, CEO Tan Teck Long warned the Middle East conflict continues to cast a cloud over the global economic outlook.
"A lot will depend on how the energy crisis triggered by the US-Iran war pans out. We continue to see K-shaped economic growth across major economies," he said in an earnings briefing.
Still, following strong loan growth in the first half, OCBC now expects high-single-digit to low-double-digit loan growth this year, up from a previous mid-single-digit forecast.
OCBC increased its interim dividend to 47 Singapore cents from 41 Singapore cents, while UOB raised its interim dividend to 88 Singapore cents per share from 85 Singapore cents.

Title: Hadi says Bersatu out of PN after Muhyiddin announced new coalition
Article:
MARANG: Bersatu's membership in Perikatan Nasional has been automatically revoked following its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's announcement that the party would form a new coalition.
Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said this was in line with the coalition's constitution.
"Bersatu has made a statement that they will form another team, so its membership within PN is automatically forfeited," he said after Friday prayers.
Last month, Muhyiddin, who is Pagoh member of parliament, reportedly said Bersatu would form a new coalition with several other parties after the Negri Sembilan state election.
He said the new alliance would involve parties in Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR), including Putra and Parti Bersepakat Hak Rakyat Malaysia (Urimai).
Hadi, who is Marang member of parliament, said PN need not issue an official notice to Bersatu as the party had effectively left the coalition by virtue of Muhyiddin's statement.
"I am of the opinion that PN does not need to issue an official letter. Our constitution states that when people join another party, they automatically leave," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly couple's 30-year drug use ends in nationwide bust
Article:
KUANTAN: An elderly married couple were among 1,209 people who tested positive for drugs during a three-day nationwide operation by the National Anti-Drug Agency.
The agency's Enforcement and Security Division director Mahadzir Elias said the husband, 64, and wife, 59, who have five children, were arrested at their home in Kuantan.
Preliminary investigations showed the couple had been involved in drug abuse for about 30 years and had never been detected or arrested before.
"We will try to help this couple overcome their addiction through treatment and rehabilitation," he told a press conference here.
He said 1,606 people were arrested during the operation, which ended yesterday, with 1,209 of them, including 56 women, testing positive for drugs.
Mahadzir said that aside from detecting drug users to treat and rehabilitate, the operation was also aimed at tracking down those who skipped bail or breached treatment and rehabilitation conditions.
On the operation in Pahang, Mahadzir said 131 of the 254 arrested were newly detected addicts.
"In this operation, we focused on drug abuse in Felda areas where 66 people tested positive for drugs in Felda areas across six districts.

Title: PH studying election setbacks as sentiment overtakes performance - Mustapha
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Public sentiment, rather than government performance, is now playing a bigger role in shaping voters' decisions, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
Mustapha, who is also Sabah Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the coalition had begun analysing the outcomes of the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.
"Undeniably, the results have some impact. We are currently studying what happened and have received several analyses.
"One finding is that sentiment is now outweighing performance. That is something that concerns us because, if we look at the country's economic performance and the performance of the state governments, these achievements no longer seem to be a major consideration for voters.
"We therefore need to reflect on whether this is healthy for the country. However, I believe we still have time to address our weaknesses," he said when asked whether the two state election results would affect PH's preparations for upcoming elections.
The Sepanggar member of parliament was speaking to reporters after the Sepanggar Parliament Madani STPM Excellence Awards programme here today.
In the recent state elections, PH won eight of the 56 seats contested in Johor and failed to retain control of Negri Sembilan after securing only 11 of the state's 36 seats.
Mustapha said the coalition also needed to examine whether initiatives and incentives introduced by both the federal and state governments were reaching the people effectively.
"There may be more fundamental issues that need to be addressed.
"We accept the election results, but we will continue improving so that we are better prepared for the next general election, which is expected to be held next year," he said.
Earlier, Mustapha said the cabinet had decided to postpone the transfer of Form Six to the higher education ministry due to issues involving infrastructure, school facilities and staffing.

Title: Man trapped, another injured after pickup truck collides with cement lorry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man was trapped inside a pickup truck while another was injured after being thrown from the vehicle following a collision with a cement lorry on the North-South Expressway near Bukit Sentosa this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.04am reporting the crash at KM397.1 of the southbound carriageway.
He said five firefighters from the Bukit Sentosa Fire and Rescue Station, along with a light fire rescue tender, were deployed to the scene.
"Upon reaching the scene, the operations commander reported that the accident involved a cement lorry and an Isuzu D-Max pickup truck.
"A man in his 30s was found trapped inside the pickup truck, while another man, also in his 30s, had been thrown from the vehicle. The latter victim sustained head injuries and a fractured right arm," he said in a statement.
Ashrul said firefighters immediately began extrication operations to free the trapped victim, while the injured man received medical assistance.
He added that the operation was brought under control at 10.58am.

Title: Taxi drivers can opt for non-S70 models under Teksi Madani
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Taxi drivers are allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70 under the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme (Teksi Madani).
The Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) said the flexibility is intended to assist applicants who already own suitable vehicles or were unsuccessful in obtaining hire-purchase financing.
The concession applies despite the Transport Ministry's policy announced on April 23, which stipulated that new applications or vehicle replacements under the programme would be voluntary and limited to the Proton S70 taxi package.
"Taxi drivers are encouraged to switch to Teksi Madani to enjoy the various incentives offered.
"However, to assist applicants who already have existing vehicles or were unsuccessful in obtaining approval for hire-purchase financing under the Teksi Madani programme, applicants are still allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70," Apad said in a statement today.
It said existing taxis that are not replaced under the programme may continue operating until they reach the maximum permitted vehicle age.
Launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on July 3, Teksi Madani enables taxi drivers to own their vehicles, ending the long-standing leasing practice in the industry.
Under the programme, the Proton S70 was designated the official taxi model, featuring a new design without rooftop taxi signs and using a special vehicle registration series beginning with the letters "GET".
Anwar also announced an additional RM10 million allocation for the Old Vehicle Replacement Matching Grant Programme following the positive response to the RM10 million allocated under Budget 2026 for the implementation of Teksi Madani.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Married couple among three charged over false Perkeso claims
Article:
SEREMBAN: Three people, including a married couple, have pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to charges of submitting and abetting in making false incentive claims under the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso).
The accused — M. S. Gunaseelan, 45, his wife S. Theen Malar, 45, and A. S. Shisman, 45 — entered their pleas after the charges were read before judge Shahrul Rizal Majid.
Gunaseelan, a business owner, was charged with making false incentive claims under the Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme using his company's name.
He was charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act, punishable under Section 24(2) of the same act.
Theen Malar and Shisman were charged under Section 28(1)(c), read together with Section 18 of the same act, punishable under Section 24(2), for abetting the offence.
The offence was allegedly committed on the night of March 11, 2024.
They each face a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the false particulars or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
MACC deputy public prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil proposed bail at RM15,000 for each accused.
The accused, who were unrepresented, requested a lower bail amount, saying they could not afford it.
The court set bail at RM12,000 each for Gunaseelan and Shisman, while bail for Theen Malar was set at RM10,000, each with one surety.
The court also ordered all three accused to report to the Seremban MACC office monthly and fixed Sept 7 for menstion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuanku Muhriz calls on Negri exco members to discharge duties with honesty, fairness
Article:
KUALA PILAH: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded the state's new executive councillors (Exco) to carry out the trust placed in them and their responsibilities with honesty, fairness and professionalism.
His Royal Highness also urged all Exco members not to abuse the powers entrusted to them for personal, family or friends' interests, especially when making decisions on the awarding of government tenders or projects.
"As I have decreed before, the country needs leaders with strong principles or persons of honour.
"Abuse of power and position will lead to injustice and fragility in the implementation of policies formulated for the benefit of the people," Tuanku Muhriz said during the appointment and swearing-in ceremony of the Negri Sembilan State Executive Council members at Istana Besar Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, here today.
Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
Also present were the Undang Luak of Sungei Ujong, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari; the Undang Luak of Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Tuanku Muhriz said the appointments represented a challenge for all the Exco members, who also serve as state assemblymen for their respective constituencies.
His Royal Highness said all the appointed leaders are responsible for formulating policies and the direction of the Negri Sembilan state administration, with the interests of the state and the people's well-being prioritised in every action and decision taken.
Tuanku Muhriz said the people have placed high expectations on the state government and, as such, every policy and plan must be implemented efficiently, transparently and effectively.
His Royal Highness added that the success of a government is not measured solely by good planning, but by its ability to deliver results that can be genuinely felt by the people.
Tuanku Muhriz also advised the new leadership to build on the achievements of the previous state government, particularly in attracting quality investments, increasing state revenue and creating more economic and employment opportunities for the people.
His Royal Highness said that Negri Sembilan had recorded high investment figures and commendable growth in state revenue, and that these achievements must be maintained, strengthened and further enhanced so that the benefits could be enjoyed by all the people of Negri Sembilan.
"At the same time, all weaknesses must be identified and continuously improved to ensure that the state administration remains excellent, high in integrity and effective," Tuanku Muhriz said.
His Royal Highness also prayed that Negri Sembilan will continue to enjoy peace, prosperity and blessings, and that all those entrusted with administering the state will always be guided towards making fair and wise decisions that prioritise the interests of the people.
The 16th Negri Sembilan State Election saw Barisan Nasional (BN) win 18 state seats while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Ismail Sabri determined to clear name despite health setback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob remains determined to clear his name as he prepares to face charges under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act later this month.
His lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, who visited the Bera member of parliament shortly after the court adjourned the charging proceedings, said he had updated Ismail Sabri on the day's developments.
Ismail Sabri, 66, is scheduled to undergo a
pacemaker procedure
at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this afternoon due to an irregular heartbeat.
"He is determined to clear his name. However, his immediate priority is his health.
"I am not a doctor and am not qualified to comment on how long his recovery will take. It will certainly take a few days, after which we will continue to monitor his progress.
"Once his condition has stabilised and he is medically cleared, we will be ready to appear in court to answer the charges against him.
"In any event, we are scheduled to appear in court on Aug 27. Hopefully, by then, he will be fit and ready to attend.
"Let us pray for his speedy recovery," he said.
Amer Hamzah arrived at the institute shortly after the court adjourned and spent about an hour meeting
Ismail Sabri
.
He said Ismail Sabri's heart arrhythmia required immediate medical attention after he suffered a fall two weeks ago.
He said doctors detected a brief episode during which his heart stopped beating for two seconds, prompting the need for the pacemaker procedure.
Asked whether MACC officers had visited Ismail Sabri at IJN today, Amer Hamzah said he had no information on the matter.
However, sources said MACC investigators visited Ismail Sabri at the institute following the court proceedings to facilitate the bail process.
Earlier, Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin fixed Aug 27 for Ismail Sabri to face the charge and have his plea recorded, subject to his health improving sufficiently for him to attend court.
The prosecution, led by deputy public prosecutor Farah Ezlin Yusop Khan, did not object to the postponement on humanitarian grounds.
Ismail Sabri had been scheduled to appear in court today to face a charge believed to be linked to his declaration of assets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two dead, including gunman, at school shooting in Thailand, officials say
Article:
BANG KRUAI: At least one teacher was killed and four other people injured by a student who opened fire at a school in Thailand north of Bangkok on Friday before killing himself, authorities said.
Lt Col Dechrapee Kongdee, Nonthaburi police chief, confirmed the casualties to Reuters and said the suspected gunman had committed suicide. Among those injured were one teacher and three students, he said.
The incident took place in the Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province. Police identified the perpetrator as a student.
In photos circulated by emergency workers, students streamed out of the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, on the northwestern outskirts of Bangkok, as ambulances operated.
In one photo, one person is seen lying down on a stretcher outside an ambulance, while another is attended to by a medic.
In the 2025 academic year, the school had an enrolment of about 3,100 students and 147 teachers, according to district authorities.
In February a teacher died and a student was injured in southern Thailand's Hat Yai district after a gunman opened fire at a school. — REUTERS

Title: Tackling stray dog menace with registration, microchipping
Article:
LETTERS:
The growing number of stray dog incidents has become a serious public safety concern, with residents across the country reporting encounters in housing areas, near schools, playgrounds, markets and public parks.
These incidents include aggressive behaviour such as chasing children, threatening pedestrians, and attacking individuals. In some cases, victims are injured not from dog bites but from falls while attempting to escape.
In Selangor, local authorities received 10,333 complaints related to stray dogs in 2025. Although approximately 95 per cent of these grievances were resolved, the high number of reports shows that stray dog management remains a challenge.
In Johor Baru, the city council captured 3,014 stray dogs in 2024 and another 2,034 dogs within the first six months of 2025, while receiving 219 public complaints during the same period.
The issue is further complicated by health risks associated with dog bites and rabies. In Sarawak, the Health Ministry recorded approximately 300 dog bite cases in Sibu in April 2025, followed by another 360 cases in May 2025.
In addition, 270 cases (75 per cent) involved owned pet dogs, while 90 cases (25 per cent) involved stray dogs, showing that irresponsible ownership is also a major contributor to public safety risks.
At the state level, Sarawak recorded nearly 14,000 animal bite cases between January and mid-September 2025, averaging about 375 incidents every week.
According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), dog bites cause tens of millions of injuries worldwide every year, with children among the most vulnerable groups. WHO also states that dogs are responsible for up to 99 per cent of human rabies transmission cases, and once symptoms appear, rabies is almost always fatal.
Therefore, preventing dog attacks is not merely an animal welfare issue but an important public health responsibility. Authorities must prioritise public safety while ensuring that animal management remains humane and responsible. One important step is a comprehensive dog registration and identification system through microchipping.
Several countries have adopted such systems to improve accountability, including Britain, Australia and Singapore. In Europe, Germany, France and Spain use microchipping to support pet identification, vaccination tracking, and enforcement of ownership responsibilities.
Microchipping creates accountability as authorities can identify the owner and take appropriate action. The Sarawak statistics clearly show that the issue involves not only stray animals but also irresponsible pet ownership.
Authorities should also establish a faster response system. Dogs that repeatedly chase children, attack pedestrians, or cause accidents should not be allowed to continue roaming freely in residential areas.
Complaints should be investigated promptly, high-risk animals should be removed from public spaces, and every incident should be recorded to identify problem areas. The success of stray dog management should not be measured by the number of dogs captured, but by whether communities become safer.
DR ASRAF MOHAMED MOUBARK
Faculty of Engineering and Built Environment, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia

ends

Title: Police recover RM96k worth of stolen cattle, arrest 10
Article:
KOTA BARU: Police have dismantled an active cattle theft syndicate operating in Kelantan following the arrest of 10 people, including two women, and the recovery of 32 stolen cattle in a series of raids in Kelantan and Terengganu.
The operations, conducted between June 17 and Aug 5, were carried out in Bachok, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Terengganu.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the arrests enabled police to solve 20 cattle theft cases in the state.
He said the operations involved four officers and 15 personnel from the Kelantan Criminal Investigation Department and the Pasir Puteh district police headquarters.
"Police raided three locations in Bachok, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Terengganu.
"The raids led to the arrest of eight men and two women, aged between 23 and 71.
"Police also seized eight mobile phones, a red plastic bag containing a bottle labelled 'Illium Xylazil-100' and a syringe, as well as a Toyota Hilux and a Perodua Kancil.
"Checks revealed that the 10 suspects had a combined total of 55 criminal records and 24 drug-related records.
"Preliminary urine screening found that one of the male suspects tested positive for methamphetamine," Yusoff said.
He said the arrests enabled police to solve 20 cattle theft cases reported across Kelantan, involving estimated losses of RM96,000.
The suspects have been taken to the respective district police headquarters for further investigation.
Yusoff said investigations are ongoing to identify other syndicate members and complete the investigation papers.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft, which carries a jail term of up to 7 years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Repeat offenders may also be liable to whipping.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN will not interfere in Bersatu Terengganu's internal affairs, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional will not interfere in Bersatu's internal affairs following the resignation of three senior Terengganu Bersatu leaders from their party positions.
PN deputy chairman and Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said PN, particularly Pas, took note of the decision as it involved elected assemblymen who remained part of the Terengganu government.
"In the context of our party, we (Pas) do not interfere too much in the affairs of other parties.
"We only take note of the decision because it involves assemblymen who were elected in the previous election.
"At the moment, they are still assemblymen because they have not left Bersatu. They have only resigned from their party positions," he said when met at a Friday sermon here today.
The Kubang Kerian assemblyman said the resignations would not affect the administration of Pas-led state governments.
"From the administrative perspective, we are maintaining all existing positions in Kelantan, Terengganu and Kedah.
"As far as I know, they are still Bersatu members. That is their decision if they decide to leave their party positions," he said.
He added that the Terengganu state administration remained unchanged, including the positions held by Bersatu representatives in the state executive council.
"As far as the Terengganu state government is concerned, the three are still exco members and they will continue to hold their positions.
"This is Bersatu's internal matter. If they were to leave the party and join another political party, whether Pas or Parti Wawasan, that would also be their own choice," he said.
Tuan Ibrahim was commenting on Terengganu Bersatu chairman Datuk Razali Idris' decision
to resign from his party post
.
Two other senior Bersatu leaders, Telemong assemblyman Mohd Zawawi Ismail and Hulu Besut assemblyman Mohd Husaimi Hussin, also announced their resignations as the party's information chief and treasurer, respectively.
It is understood that another senior party leader, Terengganu Bersatu deputy chairman Khazan Che Mat, is also expected to follow in their footsteps.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Final beach trips become family's last memories of electrocuted policeman
Article:
KOTA BARU: A policeman who was electrocuted while harvesting coconuts in Sabah had unknowingly spent his final days creating cherished memories with his family.
Lance Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, had taken his wife and their 2-year-old son to the beach several days in a row despite being exhausted from work, said his mother-in-law, Norizan Hamat.
"We never imagined he was spending precious time with his family because he would soon be gone," she said.
Norizan said Hafiz had made it a habit to video call the family daily and send photos of himself, his wife, Fatimah Syaera Zahrul Saharudin, 28, and their son, Hariz Idraqi, during their recent outings.
She said she learnt of the incident from her daughter, who told her Hafiz had been rushed to hospital after suffering an electric shock.
"Ten minutes later, my in-laws called to tell us he had passed away.
"He was a wonderful son-in-law. He called us on video every day, and we deeply feel his loss," she said when met at Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh, today.
Norizan said the family was informed that Hafiz's body was taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu for a post-mortem examination at 8am today.
He will be laid to rest at the Pangkal Kuang Muslim Cemetery in Ketereh after his remains arrive from Sabah.
Yesterday, Hafiz, who was attached to the Weston police station, was among three policemen killed after they were electrocuted while harvesting coconuts along Jalan Weston in Kampung Weston.
The other victims were Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26.
The three died after the metal pole they were using came into contact with a Sabah Electricity high-voltage power line.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asian shares pause for US jobs, oil extends gains on Middle East risk
Article:
SYDNEY: Asian shares held their breath on Friday for US jobs data that could prove pivotal for next month's interest-rate decision by the Federal Reserve, while rising oil prices served as a reminder that Middle East tensions remain far from resolved.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan held flat and was down 0.4 per cent for the week. Japan's Nikkei dropped 0.9 per cent although it was set for a weekly rise of 1.2 per cent.
South Korea's KOSPI slipped 0.5 per cent and was down 5.0 per cent for the week for a seventh straight week of declines. The index had doubled in the first half of the year, swept up by the blistering demand for AI-linked chip stocks. China's CSI 300 rose 0.2 per cent.
After bouts of volatility sparked by concerns over the durability of the AI-driven rally, investors are now squarely focused on the US payrolls report due later in the day, which could prove crucial for the interest-rate outlook. Forecasts are centred on a rise of 80,000 jobs for July after a 57,000 gain in June, with the unemployment rate forecast to hold steady at 4.2 per cent.
The stakes are high as markets cannot seem to make up their mind about how the Federal Reserve might move next month, with a rate hike seen as a coin toss.
"With yields and inflation still the key risks for stocks, we expect Friday's NFP to trade as a 'good news is bad news' print," said Michael Feroli, chief US economist at JPMorgan, adding that a strong jobs number would reinforce higher-for-longer pricing and put upward pressure on rates.
Conversely, equities may respond positively to a soft payrolls report as yields ease and policy expectations shift toward a dovish path, added Feroli.
Nasdaq futures were flat while S&P 500 futures slipped 0.1 per cent. European bourses are set for a lower open, with pan-region stock futures down 0.2 per cent.
OIL CLIMBS AGAIN
Tensions in the Middle East flared up again after Yemen's Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia, a major oil supplier. Riyadh has warned coordinated attacks by the Houthis and Iran-backed Iraqi militias were imminent.
Brent crude futures gained 1 per cent to US$83.38 a barrel, after jumping 3.8 per cent overnight. They were, however, still set for a weekly loss of 7.5 per cent and remained well off their recent peak of US$102 a barrel two weeks ago.
Iran is reviewing a preliminary bill that would bar US, Israeli and other "hostile" vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The draft bill would impose fines of up to 20 per cent of a ship's cargo value for violations of the proposed restrictions.
Higher oil prices lifted Treasury yields. The 2-year note yield held at 4.2496 per cent in Asia, after rising 7 basis points overnight, while the ten-year yield steadied at 4.6757 per cent, having gained 5 bps overnight.
The dollar was steady in Asia on Friday after bouncing overnight.
Against the Japanese yen, the dollar traded at 158.51 yen, after rising 0.4 per cent overnight to break above the 200-day average of around 158. The US jobs report could decide the next moves in the yen after last week's historic currency market intervention from Japan and the US sparked a sharp rally.
Spot gold rose 0.1 per cent to US$4,243 an ounce, while spot silver rose 0.5 per cent to US$61.78 an ounce.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil extends gains and stocks fall on fresh Hormuz worries
Article:
HONG KONG: Oil prices extended gains and stocks fell further on Friday amid fading optimism over a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as reports said Iran was planning to block US and Israeli ships from the waterway as part of a deal with Oman.
Markets had enjoyed a healthy run-up at the start of the week as US President Donald Trump called off strikes on the Islamic republic and said an agreement was close, even though Tehran denied talks had taken place.
At the same time Iran said it was close to a pact with Muscat on managing the key waterway -- which has been choked off for most of the Middle East war -- but that the US would need to end its own naval blockade of Iranian ports.
Crude prices had begun edging up Wednesday and rallied as much as four per cent Thursday as the Fars news agency said Iran would look to prevent US and Israeli vessels from using the strait in any deal with Oman.
That dampened hopes for a full reopening of the waterway -- through which a fifth of global oil and LNG passes -- and revived fears of a fresh spike in inflation and put interest rate hikes back in the picture.
Both main contracts rose around one per cent on Friday.
Equity markets were in turn mostly down, with Seoul again weighed by concerns over the AI boom while Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Wellington, Taipei and Manila were also lower. Shanghai and Singapore edged up.
That came after a pullback on Wall Street, where the Dow came off three days of record highs.
Analysts said the latest developments had traders questioning whether the week's early gains were justified.
They also come ahead of the release of key US jobs data later in the day, which will be followed next week by consumer price figures -- both of which could be crucial in the Federal Reserve's decision-making on rates.
Clark Bellin at Bellwether Wealth said the jobs figures are of major importance, adding "we will need to see a number that is not too hot and not too cold in order for the market to keep grinding higher".
And Michael Hewson of Market Insights added: "The main item of note is US (consumer price index) for July, and whether we will see further evidence of slowing price pressures.
"This matters, given the recent dissent of three (Fed policy board) members in favour of a 25-basis-point rate hike."
He added that "while we've seen a modest pull back from the recent highs (in CPI) the bigger concern is that the sustained volatility in prices could mean prices stabilise at a higher baseline.
"These are the concerns that prompted the likes of the three dissents on interest rate policy at the recent Fed meeting."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guan Eng questions Umno's commitment to Penang unity govt after Reezal's remarks
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Lim Guan Eng today criticised Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican's remarks on Umno-DAP ties in Penang, questioning whether Umno remains committed to maintaining trust within the state's unity government.
The DAP adviser described Reezal's comments as "not just unfriendly but harsh" towards its allies, DAP and PKR, accusing him of unfairly claiming that the parties were engaging in identity politics.
"By accusing DAP and PKR of engaging in identity politics, when it is BN and PN that are the real culprits, Reezal has launched an unwarranted attack on his supposed partners in the Penang state government," Lim said in a Facebook post today.
Lim questioned whether ties between Umno and DAP in the Penang government could remain cordial and free of tension if Umno became the "enemy within" by making such remarks.
"With friends like these, one does not need enemies. Particularly when former bitter foe PN has now become Umno's firm friend," he said.
Lim, who is the Bagan member of parliament and Air Putih assemblyman, also questioned whether Umno would use its position in the state government to leverage government resources to assist PN while sidelining PH.
"The time has come for our state's political leadership in PH to act decisively on behalf of our voters in defending our honour and dignity as the Penang state government and as elected leaders," he said.
Yesterday, Reezal, the Bertam assemblyman, said Umno and DAP continued to maintain cordial ties in Penang despite recent political developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
He said there had been no misunderstandings, disputes or conflicts between the two parties in the state, although differences in opinion were inevitable.
He acknowledged that developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan could have implications for the Penang unity government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 assemblymen take oath as Negri Sembilan exco members
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Ten Negri Sembilan State Executive Council (exco) members were appointed today, with two retaining their positions and eight new faces joining the state administration.
The line-up of assemblymen took their oath of office before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at the Appointment and Oath-Taking Ceremony of the Negri Sembilan State Executive Council at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today.
Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, the Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and the Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
The two assemblymen retained in the exco line-up are Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Palong assemblyman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor.
The eight new exco members are Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Chennah assemblyman Siow Kong Choon, Labu assemblywoman Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Sungai Lui assemblyman Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Gemencheh assemblyman Suhaimizan Bizar, Serting assemblyman Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
The ceremony was also attended by the Undang Luak of Sungei Ujong, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, the Undang Luak of Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid, and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Speaking at his first press conference after being sworn in as Menteri Besar on Aug 2, Ismail said the exco line-up would reflect BN's full component structure.
"We need to form a government together, and we certainly have assemblymen representing BN who are not only from Umno but also from our component parties, namely MCA and MIC.
"All of this will be given attention in the formation of the State Executive Council," he said.
Ismail, a seven-term Umno assemblyman, was sworn in as the state's 12th Menteri Besar on
Aug 2 after BN and PN secured a two-thirds majority
in the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, ending PH's eight-year administration of the state.
The 16th Negri Sembilan state election results saw BN win 18 seats while PN secured seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police seek man accused of flashing, trying to abduct 13-year-old
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Police are tracking down a man to assist investigations into the alleged sexual harassment and attempted abduction of a 13-year-old schoolgirl in Taman Sri Saujana here.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said a report on the incident was lodged last Thursday.
"Police are looking for a suspect described as a tall, thin and dark-complexioned man," he said when contacted yesterday.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 15(a)(1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
Yusof urged anyone with information on the incident or the suspect to contact investigating officer Inspector Nurul Zakiyah Daud at 011-26046234.
Earlier, a social media post by the victim's mother detailing the ordeal went viral.
According to the post, the girl was on her way to school between 6.30am and 6.40am when she was allegedly followed by a man on a motorcycle fitted with a p-hailing delivery box.
The incident was believed to have occurred from an area near the school to Taman SS6.
The man allegedly exposed himself, showed pornographic videos on his mobile phone, offered the victim money and attempted to grab her hand.
Fearing for her safety, the girl rode away on her electric scooter and headed straight to school, where she broke down in tears while recounting the incident to her teacher.
Following the incident, the mother urged parents and schoolchildren to remain vigilant and be alert to suspicious people while outdoors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Mandatory drug tests for Malaysia Airlines pilots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has introduced mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots following the arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia over alleged drug smuggling.
The group said the screening exercise covers all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots and is expected to be completed by Aug 15.
"Pilots who do not complete the screening by the stipulated date will not operate flights until they have been cleared in accordance with MAG's procedures and regulatory requirements," it said in a statement.
The move follows the
arrest of a 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot
by Indonesian authorities at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta for allegedly attempting to smuggle about 25kg of MDMA, or ecstasy, and a small amount of methamphetamine into the country.
The pilot also tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the group had zero tolerance for any form of misconduct.
"Operational safety and crew fitness for duty are non-negotiable at MAG. We take any breach of our safety standards seriously and have acted swiftly to enhance mandatory drug screening across our active pilots.
"While this isolated incident does not reflect the professionalism of the overwhelming majority of our employees, we will continue strengthening our safeguards to maintain the confidence of our passengers and stakeholders," he said.
MAG said the enhanced programme goes beyond existing industry practice and complements its current random drug testing programme.
It said mandatory drug screening would subsequently be expanded to active cabin crew.
MAG also said the enhanced measures build on its existing fitness-for-duty framework.
The current framework includes pre-employment screening, Class 1 medical certification for pilots, recurrent training, periodic alcohol and drug testing, mandatory pre-flight compliance checks, pilot fitness self-assessments under the IMSAFER checklist, as well as employee wellbeing and peer support programmes.
IMSAFER is a pilot self-assessment checklist used before a flight to evaluate fitness for duty. It stands for illness, medication, stress, alcohol, fatigue, emotion and recency.
The group said it would continue working closely with aviation, enforcement and regulatory authorities to implement recommendations, strengthen preventive measures and ensure compliance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin orders immediate probe after 3 cops electrocuted
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A comprehensive and transparent investigation has been ordered immediately to determine the actual cause of the electric shock tragedy that claimed the lives of three policemen in Beaufort yesterday.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that any weaknesses identified must be addressed immediately, while improvements must also be implemented to ensure that a similar incident does not recur.
He also expessed his condolences to the families of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee and Corporal Chiu Teck Siong.
"May God grant their families and friends the strength to face this ordeal and facilitate all their affairs," he said in a statement posted on Facebook today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the three personnel had devoted themselves to serving the religion, people and country, and describd their passing as a great loss to the Home Ministry.
In the incident at about 5.50pm yesterday, the three personnel were confirmed dead after they were believed to have suffered electric shocks while moving a 29-foot-long metal pole used to harvest coconuts outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston. —  BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's forex reserves fall to US$145.3bil in July
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves fell by around US$250 million in July to stand at US$145.34 billion at the end of that month, the central bank said on Friday, a level it said was above international standards and adequate to support external resilience.
The change in the reserves reflected foreign revenue receipts, proceeds from the government's foreign currency bond sale, as well as payments of offshore public debt and the central bank's currency interventions to shore up the rupiah, Bank Indonesia said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump signs executive order to impose 15pct tariff on polysilicon imports
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order imposing minimum import prices and a 15 per cent tariff on products made from polysilicon, a key material for solar panels and semiconductors, reported Xinhua.
The minimum import prices will be set at US$21 per kilogram for polysilicon and US$100 per kilogram for polysilicon ingots and wafers, according to a White House proclamation. The new trade measures are scheduled to take effect on Dec 4.
Trump also directed the US Commerce Department to establish a programme to encourage investment in domestic production of raw polysilicon and related downstream products.
According to a White House fact sheet, the measures are aimed at creating "a level playing field for American producers of these strategic goods", encouraging the "onshoring of these industries", and protecting "US national security and its defence and defence-adjacent industrial base".
According to the fact sheet, the US share of global polysilicon production capacity declined from 50 per cent in 2005 to less than two per cent in 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuching, Samarahan record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 7 — Kuching and Samarahan recorded unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) on Friday morning.
According to data from the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), as of 10am, Kuching recorded an API reading of 133, while Samarahan recorded 135.
Other districts in Sarawak recorded moderate readings, including Sarikei at 90, Sri Aman and Sibu at 86, Bintulu at 83, Mukah at 76 and Samalaju at 75.
An API reading between 101 and 200 is categorised as unhealthy and may pose health risks to sensitive groups, including children, the elderly and individuals with respiratory conditions.
Meanwhile, the latest data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC), updated at 5.22pm on August 6, showed widespread hotspots detected in West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
Moderate to dense smoke haze was observed drifting northwards from West Kalimantan into western parts of Sarawak. — The Borneo Post

Title: Hadi says Bersatu no longer part of Perikatan after plans for new coalition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is no longer a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Abdul Hadi said the PN constitution provides that any party choosing to join or establish another alliance would automatically cease to be a member of the coalition.
“They (Bersatu) have already stated their intention to want to form another ‘team’. They announced it themselves. They are automatically out,” he told reporters after delivering a sermon at Masjid Rusila in Terengganu today.
Abdul Hadi said there was no need for PN to issue a formal announcement on Bersatu’s status as the party had effectively removed itself from the coalition through its stated plans.
“There is no need for an official announcement. They have removed themselves by (making such an announcement),” he said.
The remarks came after PAS ended its political cooperation with Bersatu last month, although both parties remained component members of PN amid growing tensions between the two allies.
Bersatu had previously maintained that it was still part of PN, saying the coalition’s constitution required consensus among all component parties before any member could be removed.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had also announced that the party would work with several other parties to form a stronger new coalition following the Negeri Sembilan state election.
He said the proposed coalition would include parties under Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR), including Parti Putra led by Datuk Ibrahim Ali and Urimai led by P Ramasamy, and would contest the next general election.

Title: ‘No more warnings’: Immigration D-G vows action against rogue officers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department will not protect any of its officers and personnel involved in misconduct, including corruption or abuse of power, and immediate stern action will instead be taken against them without compromise.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the stance was in line with the department’s efforts to strengthen integrity and ensure that every officer carries out the trust and responsibilities entrusted to them with full professionalism.
He said the department continued to receive information on the involvement of certain personnel who were believed to be colluding in activities involving flying passports, counter setting and the irregular approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS).
“I have issued repeated warnings, but there will be no more warnings now. No more warnings and no more reminders. We will take immediate action (against officers involved in misconduct),” he said in his speech at the department’s monthly assembly here today.
Citing the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) involving the PLKS application and approval process, Zakaria said the department had received initial information on the involvement of its officers and personnel in the case.
He said the Immigration Department, together with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), was waiting for the right time to track down all those involved and ensure the case was dealt with at its root.
“Actually, on the first day the incident occurred, we were able to identify the officers involved. We knew who was involved, but I took a different approach. If I had stopped it immediately, we would not have been able to catch all those involved.
“That is why we allowed it to continue until we gathered evidence on who the culprits or masterminds behind it were. That is why I said, do not think that what happened has gone unnoticed,” he said.
Zakaria reminded department personnel to work with full integrity and stop any form of misconduct before action is taken against them.
He said every transaction involving Immigration Department matters would continue to be closely monitored to ensure any abuse of power was curbed.
“What I hope is that these incidents will serve as a lesson to other officers. If anyone is currently doing something wrong, stop before we take action. That is all. As I mentioned before, I have information,” he said.
Last Tuesday, five more Immigration officers were detained by the MACC for allegedly conspiring to hack MyIMMs in connection with the unauthorised application and approval of PLKS.
Zakaria had previously said that the department would cancel PLKS identified as having been approved by the syndicate involved in hacking the MyIMMs system through Ops Crack. — Bernama

Title: Taxi drivers can replace vehicles with models other than Proton S70, says APAD
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Taxi drivers are allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70 under the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme (Teksi Madani).
The Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) said the flexibility was provided to assist applicants who already have existing vehicles or were unsuccessful in obtaining hire-purchase financing.
This applies although the Transport Ministry’s policy announced on April 23 stipulated that new applications or taxi replacements under the programme would be voluntary and limited to the purchase of the Proton S70 taxi package offered under the programme.
“Taxi drivers are encouraged to switch to Teksi Madani to enjoy the various incentives offered.
“However, to assist applicants who already have existing vehicles or were unsuccessful in obtaining approval for hire-purchase financing under the Teksi Madani programme, applicants are still allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70,” it said in a statement today.
APAD said existing taxis that are not replaced under the programme are still allowed to operate until the specified vehicle age limit expires.
Teksi Madani, launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on July 3, enables taxi drivers to become the legal owners of new vehicles, thus ending the traditional leasing practice in the industry.
Under this transformation programme, the Proton S70 sedan was selected as the latest official taxi model, featuring a more modern image, without rooftop identification signs and using a special vehicle registration series beginning with the letters “GET”.
The Prime Minister also announced an additional allocation of RM10 million for the Old Vehicle Replacement Matching Grant Programme, specifically for the benefit of taxi drivers, following the positive response to the RM10 million allocation provided by the government under Budget 2026 for the implementation of Teksi Madani. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in Jakarta was not flying aircraft, says Malaysia Aviation Group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has clarified that the Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in a recent incident was not operating the aircraft, saying flight safety was not compromised.
MAG said the individual was a second officer travelling in the cockpit jump seat as an observer and was not the pilot flying the aircraft.
The group said the individual had also been off duty for two days before the incident, adding that the aircraft was operated safely at all times by two qualified operating pilots.
“MAG views the actions of the individual as completely unacceptable and contrary to the professional standards expected of its personnel,” the group said in a statement today.
MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said operational safety and crew fitness for duty remained non-negotiable at the group.
“We take any breach of our safety standards seriously and have acted swiftly to enhance mandatory drug screening across our active pilots.
“While this isolated incident does not reflect the professionalism of the overwhelming majority of our employees, we will continue strengthening our safeguards to maintain the confidence of our passengers and stakeholders,” he said.
MAG said it had commenced the first phase of mandatory drug screening for all pilots across its airlines, beginning with all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots.
The screening is expected to be completed by August 15, with pilots who fail to complete it by the stipulated date barred from operating flights until they are cleared in accordance with MAG’s procedures and regulatory requirements.
The group said it would also implement mandatory drug screening for all active pilots, complementing its existing random testing programme, before expanding the measure to active cabin crew.
MAG said the enhanced measures build on its existing fitness-for-duty framework, which includes pre-employment screening, Class 1 medical certification for pilots, recurrent training, periodic alcohol and drug testing, and mandatory pre-flight compliance checks covering licences, medical certification, training and recency requirements.
Before every flight, operating pilots also complete the IMSAFER assessment to evaluate each other’s physical and mental readiness for duty, complemented by Threat and Error Management (TEM) principles to identify and manage operational risks.
MAG said it would continue working closely with aviation, enforcement and regulatory authorities to implement recommendations, strengthen preventive measures and ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements across its operations and the wider aviation ecosystem.

Title: MACC-Customs anti-smuggling task force still under discussion, says department
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — The proposed joint task force between the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to combat smuggling and revenue leakages has yet to be finalised, with discussions between both agencies still ongoing.
In a response to
Malay Mail
the Customs Department said the proposed collaboration remained at the discussion stage and further details would be announced once both parties reached an agreement.
“This matter is still under discussion between the two agencies. Official information will be shared with media partners once it has been finalised,” the department said.
Yesterday the Centre to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Centre) called for greater transparency, stronger safeguards and clearer accountability measures surrounding the proposed initiative.
C4 Centre head of research and policy advocacy Arief Hamzan said while the proposed task force was a positive step towards addressing enforcement weaknesses, its role, powers and implementation mechanisms must be clearly defined.
He said clear guidelines were needed to ensure the task force could operate effectively, avoid overlapping responsibilities and deliver meaningful outcomes in tackling governance issues.
“Malaysia needs stronger transparency and accountability mechanisms to ensure government agencies can be effectively scrutinised by the public,” he said in a statement.
Arief said existing avenues for members of the public to demand accountability from government bodies remained limited, while a culture of secrecy within the bureaucracy continued to undermine public confidence.
He added that efforts to strengthen enforcement should be accompanied by broader institutional reforms, including the introduction of a Freedom of Information law and the establishment of a federal Ombudsman office to investigate and resolve public complaints against government agencies.
According to C4 Centre, the success of such reforms would depend on ensuring their frameworks aligned with international best practices to create more open, responsive and trusted public institutions.
The proposed task force was announced following discussions between MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman and Customs director-general Datuk Amran Ahmad during Amran’s courtesy visit to the anti-graft agency’s headquarters.
Abd Halim previously said the meeting involved discussions on operational challenges, including customs inspection procedures, bureaucratic issues and internal matters faced by the department.
He said both agencies also discussed mechanisms to address leakages in container management under Customs’ jurisdiction at ports nationwide.
Amran, meanwhile, said Customs had shared information on the modus operandi of syndicates attempting to evade taxes, including through smuggling activities and the falsification of information or documents to obtain approvals under certain categories.
The proposed collaboration is aimed at strengthening enforcement against offences involving container management, smuggling, document forgery and attempts to avoid tax payments.
However, questions remain over the task force’s operational structure, including its scope of authority, responsibilities, reporting mechanisms and whether its primary role will focus on monitoring, prevention or enforcement.

Title: Technician pleads not guilty to seven counts of sexually assaulting 14-year-old stepdaughter
Article:
IPOH, August 7 — A technician was charged in the Sessions Court here today with seven counts of sexually assaulting his 14-year-old stepdaughter for the past three years in Bandar Universiti, Seri Iskandar.
The 41-year-old pleaded not guilty to all the charges after they were read before Judge Jean Sharmila Jesudason.
According to the charge sheets, he was accused of committing sexual offences against the victim, who was 11 years old at the time, in May 2023 at a house in Bandar Universiti, Seri Iskandar, in the Perak Tengah district.
He was also charged with committing similar offences against the same victim in May 2024 and May 2025 at the same location.
The charges were framed under Sections 14(a), 14(b) and 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 (Act 792), which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Nor Arfahanim Azureen Arfanuddin appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyer Aliff Aiman Rusli.
Nor Arfahanim urged the court to deny bail, arguing that the accused posed a risk of interfering with the victims and prosecution witnesses.
However, if bail were to be granted, she asked the court to set it at RM32,000 for all the charges with two non-family-member sureties.
She also sought additional conditions requiring the accused to report to the nearest police station once a month and prohibiting him from contacting or disturbing the victims and witnesses.
Aliff appealed for bail to be set at a minimum of RM5,000 for all the charges, arguing that his client was the family’s sole breadwinner, earning RM2,400 a month, and had to support his 70-year-old mother and wife.
“My client is also a minor stroke patient and has no criminal record.
“The victim is currently under the care of the Welfare Department, and my client will not have any contact with the victim or the witnesses as he will be staying at his mother’s house in Pengkalan, Ipoh,” he said.
Judge Jean Sharmila granted bail of RM9,000 for all seven charges with one non-family-member surety.
The court also ordered the accused not to contact the victims or witnesses and to report to the nearest police station once a month pending the disposal of the case.
The court fixed September 17 for mention.

Title: MCMC: Under-16 social media restrictions aim to ensure greater platform accountability
Article:
SINGAPORE, Aug 7 — Malaysia’s regulatory approach to restricting social media access for users under 16 underscores the need for platforms to practice higher levels of accountability in ensuring a safe online environment, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said.
