MCMC deputy director (development) Eneng Faridah Iskandar emphasised that the restriction ensures every social media platform is taking proactive steps to protect vulnerable groups, especially underage children navigating online content.
She said platform providers, as the developers and providers of social media products, should determine the safety features within the online environment.
“Anyone who provides a product for consumption in the open market has to ensure that the product is safe and secure for use.
“People who provide online content have to be aware in terms of who is accessing their platforms,” she said on the CNA+ Talking Point programme entitled ‘Social Media Ban: Will it Work?’ on Thursday night.
According to Eneng, MCMC has seen evidence of children being harmed and often abused through their interactions on social media platforms, stressing that the issue is not unique to Malaysia but a global concern.
Nevertheless, she said the regulator is not looking to punish social media platforms; instead, it seeks to work together with them to address those committing online crimes by taking advantage of social media platforms.
“We are not portraying platforms to be the enemy. We want to work with them and hold them to a higher level of accountability and responsibility,” she added.
On June 1, Malaysia began enforcing its under-16 social media safeguards, requiring social media platforms to implement measures aimed at strengthening online safety and protecting young users.
The rule requires social media platforms with at least eight million users, such as Meta’s Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube, to implement age verification systems and prevent underage users from opening accounts. — Bernama

Title: Ten assemblymen sworn in as N. Sembilan exco members
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — Ten Negeri Sembilan assemblymen took their oaths of office today as members of the State Executive Council (Exco) before the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.
Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Palong assemblyman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor were retained as Exco members.
The new appointees are Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Chennah assemblyman Siow Kong Choon, Labu assemblywoman Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Sungai Lui assemblyman Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Gemencheh assemblyman Suhaimizan Bizar, Serting assemblyman Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
Also present at the swearing-in ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim were also in attendance.
The 16th Negeri Sembilan state election saw Barisan Nasional (BN) win 18 state seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama

Title: Tuanku Muhriz reminds new N. Sembilan exco to reject abuse of power, prioritise people
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded the state’s new executive councillors (Exco) to carry out the trust placed on them and their responsibilities with honesty, fairness and professionalism.
His Royal Highness also urged all Exco members not to abuse the powers entrusted to them for personal, family or friends’ interests, especially when making decisions on the awarding of government tenders or projects.
“As I have decreed before, the country needs leaders with strong principles or persons of honour.
“Abuse of power and position will lead to injustice and fragility in the implementation of policies formulated for the benefit of the people,” Tuanku Muhriz said during the appointment and swearing-in ceremony of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members at Istana Besar Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, here today.
Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
Also present were the Undang Luak of Sungei Ujong, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari; the Undang Luak of Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Tuanku Muhriz said the appointments represented a challenge for all the Exco members, who also serve as state assemblymen for their respective constituencies.
His Royal Highness said all the appointed leaders are responsible for formulating policies and the direction of the Negeri Sembilan state administration, with the interests of the state and the people’s well-being prioritised in every action and decision taken.
Tuanku Muhriz said the people have placed high expectations on the state government and, as such, every policy and plan must be implemented efficiently, transparently and effectively.
His Royal Highness added that the success of a government is not measured solely by good planning, but by its ability to deliver results that can be genuinely felt by the people.
Tuanku Muhriz also advised the new leadership to build on the achievements of the previous state government, particularly in attracting quality investments, increasing state revenue and creating more economic and employment opportunities for the people.
His Royal Highness said that Negeri Sembilan had recorded high investment figures and commendable growth in state revenue, and that these achievements must be maintained, strengthened and further enhanced so that the benefits could be enjoyed by all the people of Negeri Sembilan.
“At the same time, all weaknesses must be identified and continuously improved to ensure that the state administration remains excellent, high in integrity and effective,” Tuanku Muhriz said.
His Royal Highness also prayed that Negeri Sembilan will continue to enjoy peace, prosperity and blessings, and that all those entrusted with administering the state will always be guided towards making fair and wise decisions that prioritise the interests of the people.
The 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election saw Barisan Nasional (BN) win 18 state seats while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu technician loses RM58,500 in scam promising Indonesia export approval
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 7 — A women technician lost RM58,500 after falling victim to a scam offering to obtain a Food and Drug Administration (BPOM) certificate for the purpose of exporting products to Indonesia.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said on March 23, 2024, the 38-year-old victim saw an advertisement related to Jom Eksport Ke Indonesia on Wan Muhd Ali’s Facebook social page.
He said the victim, who was interested, contacted the suspect and was added to the Pt-Laara Star World WhatsApp group to be given information on how to export products to Indonesia, in addition to an online briefing via the Zoom application on May 7, 2024.
“The suspect invited the victim to participate in the Trip Titian Muhibbah programme for a fee of RM58,500 for the rental of an exhibition site and application for a BPOM certificate for kurkis, anchovies and smoked meat products in Indonesia.
“BPOM is an Indonesian government agency that functions almost the same as the Ministry of Health Malaysia and the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Division (NPRA) in terms of product regulation. For Malaysian companies wishing to export food or health products to Indonesia, BPOM registration or approval is usually required depending on the type of product,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim, who was excited to build a business network abroad, had made a payment totalling RM58,500 using her savings, but began to feel suspicious when she failed to obtain the BPOM certificate after waiting for so long.
He said the suspect also often pressured the victim to make additional payments supposedly to speed up the approval of the BPOM certificate which was in the final stages.
“After many years, the victim could no longer be patient and finally lodged a police report at 12.54pm yesterday. The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kluang college student charged with murdering newborn girl
Article:
KLUANG, Aug 7 — A college student was accused in the Magistrate’s Court here today on a charge of killing her newborn baby girl at a house here last week.
Nurshazwen Mohd Idris, 19, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Nurasidah A. Rahman.
No confession was recorded from the woman as the murder case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, Nurshazwen is charged with killing the baby girl she gave birth to at a house at Jalan Setia Mutiara 2/6, Taman Setia Mutiara here at about 10am, July 29.
She is charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment for not less than 30 years and not more than 40 years and whipping if not sentenced to death, if convicted.
The court did not grant bail to the accused and set October 8 for mention of the case pending chemical, psychological and post-mortem reports.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Abd Rahman, while the accused was not represented by a lawyer.
Previously, police arrested a couple who were also college students, both aged 19, to assist in the investigation into the murder of a baby girl who was found with several stab wounds in the toilet bowl of a rented house.
The student also gave birth to a baby girl at a hospital after doctors who conducted an examination found that there was another twin baby still in her womb.
Yesterday, the police released the student’s boyfriend to be used as a prosecution witness. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Aviation Group mandates pilot drug tests after off-duty crew member’s Jakarta drug arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has commenced mandatory drug screening for all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots and will implement stricter screening for all active pilots, going beyond current industry practice.
The parent company of Malaysia Airlines Bhd has begun screening pilots across its airlines, with the exercise expected to be completed by August 15, 2026.
“Pilots who do not complete the screening by the stipulated date will not operate flights until they have been cleared in accordance with MAG’s procedures and regulatory requirements,” the group said in a statement today.
In addition, MAG said the group will implement mandatory drug screening for all active pilots, complementing its existing random testing programme and will subsequently be expanded to active cabin crew.
“This swift response reflects the high level of concern with which MAG views the recent incident involving the detention of its pilot, as the group maintains zero tolerance for any form of misconduct,” it said.
On July 29, a Malaysian pilot was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle a large quantity of drugs, including over 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25 kilogrammes, into Indonesia.
The 39-year-old man had flown Malaysian Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta and was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport.
MAG confirmed that the individual concerned was a second officer travelling in the cockpit jump seat as an observer and was not the pilot flying the aircraft.
“The individual had also been off duty for two days preceding the incident. The aircraft was operated safely at all times by two qualified operating pilots,” it said.
The group viewed the individual’s actions as completely unacceptable and contrary to the professional standards expected of its personnel.
MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said operational safety and crew fitness for duty were non-negotiable at MAG.
“We take any breach of our safety standards seriously and have acted swiftly to enhance mandatory drug screening across our active pilots.
“While this isolated incident does not reflect the professionalism of the overwhelming majority of our employees, we will continue strengthening our safeguards to maintain the confidence of our passengers and stakeholders,” he said.
According to MAG, the set of operating pilots completes the IMSAFER assessment before every flight to evaluate each other’s physical and mental readiness for duty, which is complemented by Threat and Error Management (TEM) principles to identify and manage operational risks.
IMSAFER is a pilot self-assessment checklist used before flight to evaluate fitness for duty. It stands for illness, medication, stress, alcohol, fatigue, emotion and recency.
It added that MAG would continue working closely with aviation, enforcement and regulatory authorities to implement recommendations, strengthen preventive measures and ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements across its operations and the wider aviation ecosystem. — Bernama

Title: Perak authorities probe suspected Irrawaddy dolphin carcass washed ashore in Ban Pecah
Article:
IPOH, Aug 7 — The Perak Fisheries Department will send a team to investigate the authenticity of a viral claim regarding the discovery of an Irrawaddy dolphin carcass at Ban Pecah, Tanjung Piandang, today.
Its director, Mohd Ghazali A. Manap, said it had yet to receive any official complaint regarding the discovery of the marine mammal, and only became aware of the incident after a 27-second video went viral on social media.
“A team from the Kuala Kurau Fisheries Office was sent to the location this morning to confirm whether the marine mammal carcass is still there or whether the video is an old recording.
“If the dolphin carcass is found, we will collect it and conduct a post-mortem at the Fisheries Research Centre to determine the cause of death. After that, the carcass will be preserved so that its skeleton can be kept as a specimen,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
On Tuesday (August 4), the video showing the discovery of the marine mammal carcass was shared on Instagram and attracted the attention of netizens, with many expressing concern over the condition of marine life in the waters there.
Elaborating on the discovery of the dolphin carcass, Mohd Ghazali said that based on observations from the video, the marine mammal was estimated to be about two metres long and between seven and nine years old.
He added that the discovery of the species in the area was not unusual as the waters are among the routes used by the marine mammals in search of food.
“The mammal’s actual identity cannot be determined based only on the video recording, but requires further examination of the actual specimen.
“If just based on records, the mammal can grow to a maximum length of about three metres, has a lifespan of up to 30 years and usually reaches maturity between seven and nine years of age,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Home minister orders immediate probe into deaths of three cops in Beaufort electric shock tragedy
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — A comprehensive and transparent investigation has been ordered immediately to determine the actual cause of the electric shock tragedy that claimed the lives of three Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel in Beaufort yesterday.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that any weaknesses identified must be addressed immediately, while improvements must also be implemented to ensure that a similar incident does not recur.
He also expessed his condolences to the families of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee and Corporal Chiu Teck Siong.
“May Allah SWT grant their families and friends the strength to face this ordeal and facilitate all their affairs,” he said in a statement posted on Facebook today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the three personnel had devoted themselves to serving the religion, people and country, and described their passing as a great loss to the Home Ministry (KDN).
In the incident at about 5.50pm yesterday, the three personnel were confirmed dead after they were believed to have suffered electric shocks while moving a 29-foot-long metal pole used to harvest coconuts outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston. — Bernama

Title: ‘If the head is gone, the tail will follow’: Bersatu leaders resign in Terengganu
Article:
MARANG, Aug 7 — Terengganu Bersatu was left reeling after Datuk Razali Idris announced his resignation as state chief, a post he has held for a decade.
Razali, who is also a state executive councillor and one of Bersatu’s founding members in 2016, confirmed he had submitted his resignation letter to party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin on July 16.
“So far, the party headquarters, including Muhyiddin, has yet to confirm or decide whether to accept or reject the resignation,” he told
Berita Harian
(BH) yesterday.
He further confirmed he would step down as Marang division chief in mid August, citing the need to settle party matters at the division level.
“I am only resigning as state chief and division chief, but I remain a party member,” he said.
According to BH, two other senior leaders — Telemong assemblyman Mohd Zawawi Ismail and Hulu Besut assemblyman Mohd Husaimi Hussin — also announced their resignations.
Another top leader, Bersatu Kuala Nerus division chief and deputy speaker of the Terengganu assembly Khazan Che Mat, who is also the party’s deputy state chief, is expected to follow suit.
Khazan declined to elaborate but offered a metaphor: “If the head is gone, the tail will follow.”
He told BH, “I joined Bersatu in 2016 at Razali’s invitation. If he resigns, why should I continue holding office?”

Title: Former Chief Justice Mohamed Eusoff Chin dies at 91
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin passed away today at the age of 91.
The matter was confirmed by former Malaysian Bar president Mohamad Ezri Abdul Wahab in a text message to Bernama.
He said a message posted by the late Mohamed Eusoff’s daughter, Zuliana, stated that her father passed away at 1am today.
Funeral prayers will be held at Masjid Al-Hidayah, Kelana Jaya, before he is laid to rest at Tanah Perkuburan Islam Seksyen 9, Kota Damansara.
Mohamed Eusoff served as Malaysia’s second Chief Justice from September 1994 to December 2000. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia-Thailand border smuggling drops after illegal jetty crackdown
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 7 — The closure of illegal bases along the Malaysia-Thailand border has disrupted the movement and transit network of smuggling syndicates, thus contributing to a significant decrease in smuggling cases detected in Kelantan.
Kelantan Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) director Hanif Yusabra Yusof said the closure of illegal routes has caused syndicates to face difficulties in carrying out smuggling activities as their access and transit routes have been affected.
“When compared to the situation before the illegal base was closed and today, the decrease is very significant in terms of smuggling cases that we detect and arrest.
“When access for smuggling is closed, the control of the enforcement authorities becomes better and it helps enforcement operations,” he told Bernama recently.
He said the KPDN has also strengthened control in border areas through static deployment of personnel at petrol stations in addition to continuous patrols as part of routine operations.
He said the operation was carried out seven days a week with a focus on border areas to curb the leakage and smuggling of controlled goods, especially subsidised fuel.
Commenting on Thailand’s proposal to build a fort in the border area, Hanif Yusabra said the Kelantan KPDN welcomed the move because it was expected to strengthen cross-border control and further complicate the movement of smuggling syndicates.
Meanwhile, a recent Bernama survey in the town of Sungai Golok, Narathiwat in Thailand found the sale of petrol and diesel believed to be smuggled from Malaysia has been decreasing compared to before the closure of illegal bases along the border.
Earlier, the fuel was easily found for sale in several locations.
The survey results found that there were still traders offering petrol and diesel in bottles and plastic drums in several locations, but the amount was much smaller and they were no longer sold openly as before.
The survey also found that most locations previously believed to be transit and fuel sales points appeared deserted, thus illustrating the impact of the closure of illegal bases on the supply chain of cross-border smuggling activities. — Bernama

Title: Man found dead in Gua Musang cave
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Aug 7 — An elderly man was found dead in a cave near a resort in Kampung Pulai, here, last night.
Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Operations commander Che Razak Harun said his department received a call at 9.41pm before 13 members with two engines and two four-wheel drive vehicles were rushed to the location.
He said upon arrival at 9.57pm, firefighters found the victim, estimated to be in his 70s, unconscious in the cave.
“Members used a stretcher and lights to carry the victim out before Health Ministry officials confirmed that the man had died,” he said when contacted today.
He said the victim’s body was then handed over to the police for further action, while the operation was brought under control at 10.10 pm before being completely ended at 10.48 pm. — Bernama

Title: Ex‑PM Ismail Sabri in IJN, corruption charge postponed to Aug 27
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob will not be charged at the Sessions Court in Kuala Lumpur today, as he is currently warded at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin allowed a request from Ismail Sabri’s lawyer to postpone the reading of charges against him to August 27, in light of his health condition and because the prosecution did not object.
While Ismail Sabri’s case was called up in court this morning, his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad informed the judge that the politician had been admitted to IJN since yesterday.
Amer said Ismail Sabri was at the Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission’s (MACC) headquarters yesterday to record his statement, accompanied by his lawyer Ragunath Kesavan.
“He did experience health issues that have been informed to the relevant MACC officers, they were aware of his condition in the recording of statement, and from there he had to be rushed to IJN,” he said.
Following Ismail Sabri being admitted to IJN yesterday, Amer Hamzah said they have managed to obtain confirmation from the doctor in charge and that a copy of that letter has been given to the prosecution: “Based on that confirmation, our client has health issue, where the latest Holter study has revealed there is possible arrhythmia that requires further investigation.”
“This morning as well on the way to court, we have confirmed with our client to ascertain his condition. And we were informed he’s supposed to undergo a procedure this afternoon,” he said, adding that it is a pacemaker procedure.
Amer said this is a rare situation where it would be appropriate to defer the reading of charges and recording of plea to another date.
As Ismail Sabri would have to be warded after undergoing his procedure this afternoon, Amer Hamzah proposed that the court postpone the reading of charges to August 27: “And hopefully by that time he will be fit and ready to enter a plea in court.”
Amer Hamzah said Ismail Sabri is still under MACC bail and there is no issue of him absconding.
Deputy public prosecutor Farah Ezlin Yusof Khan then said, “it is only fair on humanitarian grounds” for the prosecution not to object to the application to postpone the case to August 27, since Ismail Sabri would not be able to appear in court due to his health condition and because he is currently under MACC bail.
Amer Hamzah then expressed appreciation to the prosecution for understanding his client’s current situation.
The prosecution was also represented today by deputy public prosecutors Ifa Sirrhu Samsudin and Nurul Qistini Qamarul Abrar, while Ismail Sabri was also represented today by lawyers Datuk Seri Rajan Navaratnam, Ragunath, Joshua Tay, Tan Xu Yin, Aswath Ramakhrisnan and Sanjey G. Sangkar.
Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, lawyer representing Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, speaking to the media at a press conference in Kuala Lumpur on August 7, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Later, Amer Hamzah told reporters that “it is not practical for the charge to be read out at IJN” due to his client’s health condition and the pacemaker procedure that he has to undergo today.
Amer Hamzah said Ismail Sabri previously also had health issues, noting that his client had a fall two weeks ago and was admitted to Pantai Hospital and was actually scheduled for a check-up with IJN next Monday.
Ragunath told reporters that his client was at the MACC headquarters from 9am to 6pm yesterday.
Yesterday, Ismail Sabri was reported to be expected to face charges today under the Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission (MACC) Act in relation to the declaration of assets.
Former Umno vice president Ismail Sabri, 66, is the Bera MP and was Malaysia’s ninth prime minister from August 2021 to October 2022.
The MACC had in February 2025 arrested four of Ismail Sabri’s officers, and also seized about RM170 million in cash and other currencies, 16kg of gold bars valued at RM7 million, jewellery, and luxury watches from his aide’s house.
Ismail Sabri had appeared at the MACC headquarters multiple times between March to May 2025 to give his statement.
On October 1, 2025, the Sessions Court had ordered over RM169 million in cash to be forfeited to the Malaysian government, as both Ismail Sabri and his aide did not challenge the forfeiture and no other party challenged the forfeiture.

Title: Lim Guan Eng slams Reezal’s ‘cordial ties’ claim, says Umno acting as enemy within
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Lim Guan Eng has hit back at Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican over remarks describing ties between Umno and DAP in Penang as “cordial and tension free”.
Lim said Reezal’s comments were not only unfriendly but harsh towards supposed allies in the state government. He argued it was wrong to accuse DAP and PKR of indulging in identity politics, claiming instead that Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) were the real culprits.
“Can ties between Umno and DAP in the Penang government remain cordial and tension free when Umno behaves like an ‘enemy within’ by making such unwarranted attacks? With friends like these, one does not need enemies,” Lim wrote in a Facebook post today.
He noted that Umno, once a bitter foe of PN, had now become its firm ally.
“Will Umno use its current position to tap Penang’s government resources to help PN and sideline Pakatan Harapan (PH)?” he asked.
Lim said the time had come for PH’s leadership in Penang to act decisively on behalf of voters.
“We must defend our honour and dignity as the state government and as elected leaders,” he added.

Title: Malaysia condemns Israeli violations at Al-Aqsa, settlement expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia condemned the continued violations at Al-Aqsa Mosque and the expansion of Israeli illegal settlements during a ministerial meeting of Arab and Islamic countries on Wednesday.
The Ministerial Meeting in Support of Jerusalem and Its Holy Sites was held in Jordan to discuss the escalation in Occupied Jerusalem and to formulate a common position in response.
Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry reemphasised that Jerusalem is an integral part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory and strongly rejected any attempt to alter its legal, historical, demographic, and religious status.
“Malaysia reaffirmed its support for the Hashemite Custodianship over the Islamic and Christian Holy Sites in Jerusalem, and reiterated its unwavering support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent State of Palestine on the 4 June 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital,” the ministry also known as Wisma Putra said in a Facebook post on Thursday.
Malaysia was represented at the meeting by Wisma Putra Deputy Secretary-General of Multilateral Affairs, Datuk Dr Ahmad Faisal Muhamad.
Participants discussed steps to be taken to preserve the city’s legal and historical status, safeguard its Islamic and Christian holy sites, and advance coordinated international efforts towards a just and lasting peace based on the two-state solution.
Among the measures agreed upon include the setting up of a a media platform to document and expose Israeli violations against holy sites and worshippers, as well as their catastrophic repercussions.
Another measure is to jointly mobilise an effective international response to compel Israel as the occupying power to cease its escalatory and illegitimate practices, measures, and policies, and respect the historic and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its holy sites. — Bernama

Title: College student drowns while swimming with friends in Dungun
Article:
DUNGUN, Aug 7 — A Kolej Ketengah student in Bandar Al-Muktafi Billah Shah was found drowned after swimming with nine friends at Sungai Loh in Kampung Jongok Batu, Hulu Dungun, near here yesterday.
Bandar Al-Muktafi Billah Shah Fire and Rescue Station Operations Commander, Senior Fire Officer I Kamal Suhaimi Abdullah, said the victim, Ahmad Al Hafiz Asri Ahmad, 19, was found by volunteer fire brigade members trapped between rocks about 10 metres from where he was reported missing at 5.20pm.
He said the victim, from Kampung Jaya Baru, Jalan Felda Bukit Bading in Ajil, Hulu Terengganu, was believed to have drowned after jumping into the river and failing to resurface at about 4.40pm.
“Initial information from the victim’s friends indicated that the victim, who was pursuing a Diploma in Islamic Tourism Management at Kolej Ketengah, had gone to Sungai Loh with nine friends for a swim at about 11 am,” he said in a statement last night.
Eight firefighters and three volunteer fire brigade members were involved in the search and rescue operation.
The victim’s body was later taken to the Forensic Unit of Dungun Hospital for a post-mortem. — Bernama

Title: Bodies of three Beaufort policemen sent to Kota Kinabalu for post-mortems
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The bodies of three police officers who died, believed to have been electrocuted in Beaufort, were yesterday taken to the Forensic Department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital here from Beaufort Hospital early this morning for post-mortem.
A Bernama observation at the hospital compound found that the three vans carrying the bodies arrived at 1.10am accompanied by several Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) patrol vehicles from the Beaufort, Papar, Penampang and Kota Kinabalu District Police Headquarters.
Beaufort district police chief Supt Champin Piuh when contacted said the bodies would undergo post-mortem and documentation process before being handed over to the next of kin.
“After all the formalities are completed, the bodies will be sent back to their respective hometowns accompanied by police officers from the Beaufort IPD,” he said.
The three victims, who were on duty at the Weston police station, are Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, originally from Sarawak; Lance Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, 29, from Kelantan; and Lance Corporal Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26, from Terengganu.
In the incident at about 5.50pm yesterday, the three personnel were confirmed dead after they were believed to have been electrocuted while removing a 29-foot iron pole used to harvest coconuts outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston. — Bernama

Title: Nurul Izzah steps aside as PKR deputy to pursue studies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Nurul Izzah Anwar said her decision to relinquish the post of PKR deputy president was made after careful consideration to allow her to focus on further studies and continue serving the community, which need not necessarily be tied to politics.
In a Facebook post yesterday, she said she would remain a PKR member and continue supporting the party’s struggle towards building a better Malaysia.
“I will continue to remain a Keadilan (PKR) member, supporting the struggle for a better Malaysia led by the party’s leadership under Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim together with its grassroots,” she said.
Nurul Izzah also expressed her appreciation to Anwar and the party leadership for respecting her decision to step down as deputy president.
She also thanked PKR members, leaders at all levels and fellow party members for the trust, advice, prayers and sacrifices they had extended throughout her political journey.
In the same post, Nurul Izzah said she was confident that PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who will serve as acting deputy president, together with Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari as PKR election director, would be able to discharge the responsibilities entrusted to them with wisdom, prudence and diligence.
“I pray that all their affairs will be eased as they shoulder these responsibilities,” she said.
She also expressed her hope of meeting party members at the PKR National Congress, which will be held in Melaka on August 15 and 16.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said in a statement yesterday that the party’s Central Leadership Council (MPP) had agreed to grant Nurul Izzah temporary leave from her duties as deputy president, effective after the PKR National Congress until further notice.
Fahmi said PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail would serve as acting deputy president, adding that the decision was made following a meeting to discuss Nurul Izzah’s request to step down from the post. — Bernama

Title: High Court quashes RM313.8m tax bill against Daim’s widow Na’imah
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 7 — The High Court here yesterday allowed the judicial review application by Toh Puan Na’imah Abdul Khalid, the wife of former Finance Minister Tun Daim Zainuddin, to quash an additional tax assessment notice amounting to RM313.8 million issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
Judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad ruled that the IRB had acted beyond its jurisdiction under the Income Tax Act 1967 when it issued the additional assessment notice dated August 13, 2024, for the 2018 assessment year.
She said the Income Tax Act 1967 applied only to income earned in Malaysia and foreign-sourced income remitted into Malaysia, while the assets in dispute were Na’imah’s properties abroad and did not constitute income received in the country.
“Based on the reasons stated, the court hereby allows the applicant’s judicial review application with costs,” she said in the grounds of judgment.
The judge also ruled that the additional assessment notice was unlawful as the amount of share ownership involved had previously been assessed through the joint assessment of Na’imah and the late Daim for the 2018 assessment year.
According to Evawani Farisyta, the IRB’s action had resulted in double taxation, contrary to the provisions of the Income Tax Act 1967.
She also ruled that the market value of assets abroad could not be treated as taxable income solely by reason of ownership, as such a provision is not provided for under the Income Tax Act 1967.
The judge said that if the IRB was of the view that income had not been declared when the assets were acquired in the 1990s, the appropriate assessment should have been made for that period rather than for the 2018 assessment year.
Evawani Farisyta also found it unreasonable for the IRB to require Na’imah to submit documents pertaining to assets acquired more than 20 years ago, as the Income Tax Act 1967 only mandates that taxpayers keep such records for seven years.
She held that the failure to furnish documents that were no longer legally obliged to keep could not justify the issuance of an additional assessment notice.
Na’imah was represented by S. Saravana Kumar, Nur Amira Ahmad Azhar and Dharshini Sharma, while the IRB was represented by senior revenue counsel Marina Ibrahim and Fatimah Roslan.
In her application, Na’imah sought to challenge the additional assessment notice issued by the IRB on August 13, 2024, over three overseas assets allegedly used in the settlement of loans between Ilham Baru Sdn Bhd and Ilham Tower Sdn Bhd and Welberton Private Equity Corp under a settlement agreement dated January 18, 2018.
Previously,  the same court dismissed an application by Na’imah for an interim stay against an order requiring her to pay RM313.82 million in income tax arrears to the IRB.
The court found no exceptional circumstances warranting the stay, emphasising that the respondent (IRB) holds the legal authority to enforce tax collection under the Income Tax Act 1967.
However, on October 28, 2024, the Court of Appeal unanimously allowed Na’imah’s application for a temporary stay of payment of RM313.82 million in income tax arrears to the IRB pending the disposal of her appeal. — Bernama

Title: Anwar orders full probe into deaths of three Beaufort policemen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent, and prompt investigation into the incident that claimed the lives of three police officers, believed to be due to electrocution in Kampung Weston, Beaufort, Sabah, yesterday.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said that the investigation is crucial to identify the cause of the tragic incident and to ensure that corrective measures are taken to prevent similar occurrences from happening again.
“I have requested for a comprehensive, transparent, and prompt investigation to be conducted to determine the cause of this tragic incident. Improvements must be implemented so that a tragedy like this does not repeat,” he said.
The prime minister also extended his deepest condolences to families of the victims and the entire Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) force over the loss of the three personnel.
“Their service and sacrifice in maintaining the peace and security of the country will always be remembered,” he stated.
According to preliminary information from the Operations Centre of the Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), the three deceased police officers were identified as Chiu Teck Siong, 40; Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, 29; and Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26.
Previously, the incident went viral through several video recordings on social media showing three individuals lying on the road, while members of the public and others were present at the scene. — Bernama

Title: Infant injured as Toyota Alphard and Hilux collide in Seri Kembangan, two adults hurt
Article:
SERI KEMBANGAN, Aug 7 — A five month old boy suffered facial injuries in a collision involving two multi purpose vehicles (MPVs) and a four wheel drive at Taman Universiti Indah last night.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the emergency call was received at 9.44pm,
Harian Metro
(HM) reported
He said the accident involved a Toyota Alphard and a Toyota Hilux.
“There were three people in the Hilux — a 26 year old male driver and a 22 year old female passenger, both with minor injuries. The five month old boy travelling with them sustained facial injuries,” he said in a statement to HM.
Ashrul said the woman and her baby were taken to the hospital for further treatment.

Title: Three policemen die after suspected electrocution in Beaufort
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — Three policemen were killed, suspected of having been electrocuted along Jalan Weston, Kampung Weston, Beaufort yesterday afternoon.
Several videos of the incident quickly went viral on social media, showing three men lying on the road as onlookers gathered nearby.
In a statement, the Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said it received a distress call at 5.56pm.
Following this, the Beaufort Fire and Rescue Station deployed a Fire Rescue Tender with a team of seven to the location, approximately 28 kilometres from the station.
“The initial report stated that three victims had been electrocuted along Jalan Weston, Kampung Weston, before the fire brigade was deployed to carry out rescue operations,” the statement read.
Operations Commander, PBK I Irwan Abdul, led the team, assisted by the Royal Malaysia Police and Sabah Electricity.
Details regarding the victims’ identities and the cause of the incident are still under investigation and will be updated from time to time.
Meanwhile, in its latest update, the Sabah JBPM Operations Centre identified the three police officers killed as Chiu Teck Siong, 40, Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, 29, and Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26.
According to initial investigations, witnesses told authorities that the victims had been trying to knock down coconuts using a metal pole when it accidentally struck an overhead power cable.
“Sabah Electricity personnel managed to cut off the power supply at 6.45pm, after which the fire brigade and police retrieved their bodies,” he said.
The operation was called off at 7.45pm after the scene was cleared of any further dangers.
Sabah police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun confirmed the incident and said the officers involved were stationed at the Weston Police Station in Beaufort.
“Police have opened an investigation paper to determine the exact cause of the incident. Autopsies will be conducted before the remains are handed over to the next of kin,” he said when contacted last night.
Meanwhile, Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd said in a statement that a detailed investigation into the fatal incident is being conducted.
The utility company confirmed that its technical team was deployed to the scene upon receiving the information, to ensure the area was safe.
“Sabah Electricity extends its deepest condolences to the families of the victims and the entire PDRM personnel, and shares in their grief over this loss,” it said.
Sabah Electricity urged the public not to speculate, and pledged full cooperation with the authorities and appropriate action based on the probe’s findings. — Bernama

Title: Ismail Sabri expected to face MACC charge at IJN, Sessions Court judge to preside
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob is scheduled to face a charge under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act this morning at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT), the Bera MP’s case will be heard before Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin at the hospital.
Ismail’s lawyer Ragunath Kesavan confirmed his client had been admitted to IJN. The prosecution intends for his plea to be recorded at the institute, he told FMT.
